transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Evelyn (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Priya (GTS InfoSec), Tom (Procurement), Lena (Cloud Architect)

Summary (auto): quick run through of SIG/CAIQ, questions on data residency, KMS keys, and production audit logs. Action items captured.

00:00:03 Evelyn: ok, hello everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Evelyn from Redwood Inference, with Marco, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:00:10 Priya: good, thanks. We got the invite, we've been looking at the SIG and had a few higher risk controls we wanted to discuss.
00:00:17 Marco: great, yeah we'll run through the CAIQ mapping we pre-populated, point to where the evidence lives, and note any gaps. Quick note — transcription may flip "Redwood Private" to "Redwood Privet" in some places, apologies if that shows up.
00:00:30 Tom: sounds good, procurement will want to confirm contract, but first we need evidence that aligns to our vendor risk form.
00:01:02 Marco: jumping in — first page, SOC 2 Type II, we've got the report and the control matrix. The SOC report link we shared is a redacted PDF but includes test period and auditor statement. For CAIQ rows that ask for encryption at rest, we reference our KMS key management doc.
00:01:25 Priya: when you say KMS key management, is that customer-managed keys or do you use Redwood-managed KMS? Our policy prefers customer keys for regulated workloads.
00:01:38 Evelyn: great question. We support both. Hosted deployments use Redwood-managed keys by default (we use cloud KMS with envelope encryption), but for Private or Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS/HSM via customer-managed keys — we have a documented integration flow.
00:01:55 Lena: and that work with our on-prem HSM? we run YubiHSM in some clusters.
00:02:03 Marco: yes, we have customers using HSMs; the integration is via standard KMIP or cloud HSM connectors depending on environment. We'll include the checklist. Also note, for customer-managed keys we can provide guidance on key rotation, access policies, and audit logging.
00:02:25 Priya: okay, and data residency — we have EU-only data requirements for a portion of our workloads. How do you guarantee data stays in region?
00:02:34 Evelyn: we offer region pinning on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted API we also provide region-aware routing and contractual commitments for data handling — but for strict EU-only requirements we recommend Private (VPC) or Dedicated in an EU region.
00:02:50 Tom: procurement will want to see proof of data egress controls and where backups are stored.
00:02:58 Marco: understood — we'll attach the backup/resiliency page and storage location doc. We'll also share S3 bucket encryption screenshots where applicable.
00:03:15 Priya: on audit logs — can you show the schema and retention windows? customer wants 7 years for some logs.
00:03:24 Marco: currently audit logs are retained for 2 years by default in Hosted, configurable for Dedicated and Private. For Private we leave retention to customer policy. We can produce anonymized samples of the audit log that show event types (auth, model loads, admin actions). Are sample logs okay if we redact PII?
00:03:45 Priya: yes redacted samples are fine, just need to see the fields and timestamps.
00:03:53 Evelyn: note that the logs include request id, user id (if SSO mapped), action, resource id, timestamp, and result code. The transcript may show "k v cash" when Marco says KV cache, haha — small transcription glitch.
00:04:10 Marco: moving on to RBAC and SSO — we support SAML 2.0 / OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and granular RBAC with role templates. We can map SAML groups to Redwood roles.
00:04:23 Lena: is SCIM available for Private too? we prefer SCIM so we can automate provisioning.
00:04:28 Marco: yes, SCIM is available across Dedicated and Private; for Hosted it is supported as well for enterprise customers. We'll attach the SCIM attribute mapping doc.
00:04:40 Tom: procurement question: does Redwood provide ISO 27001 cert?
00:04:45 Evelyn: we have ISO 27001 alignment work in progress, currently SOC 2 Type II is our primary audited report — ISO cert expected mid-2026 (estimated). We'll mark that as a future deliverable in the CAIQ.
00:05:00 Priya: ok. for SIG items that require evidence (like access reviews), what do you typically provide?
00:05:06 Marco: for access reviews we provide screenshots of our admin console, export of periodic user access reviews, and meeting minutes if required. For privileged access we show RBAC configs and proof of periodic reviews. For vendor attestation questions we supply our security policy docs.
00:05:25 Priya: sometimes the vendor questionnaire asks for specific config values, like minimum password length or MFA enforcement — do you have a table of baseline settings?
00:05:34 Marco: yes, we have a security settings baseline table; password policies and MFA enforcement screenshots. For SSO enforced logins, we can show that MFA is enforced via IdP.
00:05:50 Tom: I'd like to call out one requirement — our legal team needs an archival chain showing evidence retention. Do you keep timestamped, signed artifacts?
00:05:59 Marco: we can provide signed artifacts (hashes) for audit evidence exports and retention metadata. We'll include an example export with SHA256 checksums.
00:06:12 Priya: the SIG also asks about vulnerability management cadence and patch timelines. What's your SLA?
00:06:18 Evelyn: we run weekly vulnerability scans, high severity issues have a 72-hour remediation target, criticals are treated as emergencies; we capture patch windows and maintenance notices in the console. We'll include a recent VMR summary.
00:06:35 Lena: network segmentation question — in Private deployment can we force egress via our firewall and limit vendor access?
00:06:43 Marco: absolutely, Private deployments are deployed inside your VPC/subnet and we can configure egress rules and jump host access for vendor support. We'll provide a runbook for support access escalation with ticketing and time-boxed sessions.
00:06:58 Tom: procurement note: competitor BigCloudAI asked about lower pricing for embedded models — how are you positioned there?
00:07:06 Evelyn: we compete on predictable unit economics and operational controls; competitors may underprice but lack the enterprise-grade observability and private deployment option.
00:07:20 Priya: back to CAIQ specifics — there were a few rows we left blank in your pre-populated sheet, like A1.2 and A8.5 — can we go through those?
00:07:28 Marco: sure, A1.2 is around privileged account management — we reference our PAM integration doc and JIT access controls. For A8.5 (data transfer and encryption in transit), we indicated TLS 1.2+ and mTLS options for internal service-to-service communication.
00:07:50 Priya: do you support customer-controlled key rotation schedule? policy requires rotation every 90 days for some workloads.
00:07:58 Marco: with customer-managed keys you control rotation. For Redwood-managed keys we recommend a rotation schedule aligned with best practices; we'll document current rotation frequency.
00:08:12 Priya: excellent. any items we should flag as "high risk" earlier?
00:08:17 Evelyn: the typical flags are hosted backups location and default key ownership for hosted services — if those are deal-breakers we steer customers to Dedicated or Private.
00:08:30 Tom: procurement will want a brief one-page evidence summary they can attach to the VRM.
00:08:36 Evelyn: we'll produce a one-page vendor evidence summary with links to the detailed bundle.
00:08:44 Priya: one more — incident response. If there's a data incident, what's your notification SLA and post-incident evidence?
00:08:52 Marco: we have contractual incident notification SLAs (72 hours initial notification for incidents impacting confidentiality). Post-incident we provide a root cause analysis, timeline, and evidence of remediation. We'll paste the incident response playbook excerpt.
00:09:08 Lena: would love to see a sample RCA redacted.
00:09:11 Marco: we can include a sanitized RCA.
00:09:18 Evelyn: okay let's capture next steps — we'll upload the SOC2, CAIQ mapping, SCIM mapping, audit log samples, and runbook items.
00:09:26 Priya: thanks. also can you include the encryption-at-rest architecture diagram?
00:09:30 Marco: yes. We'll include that.
00:09:35 Tom: procurement: timeline for finalizing contract once VRM is satisfied? about 2-3 weeks after evidence is accepted.
00:09:43 Evelyn: sounds reasonable. We'll aim to turn around evidence in 3-4 business days and then iterate.
00:09:50 Priya: ok good.
00:09:55 Speaker 6: (murmur)
00:10:05 Marco: i'll just note a couple of small CAIQ mapping items — some of the questionnaire rows reference endpoint-level telemetry and we use a combination of application logs plus infra telemetry; the mapping doc spells out which logs satisfy which row.
00:10:22 Priya: perfect. if we flag anything as "needs compensating control" will you provide mitigations?
00:10:28 Evelyn: yes we'll propose compensating controls where direct evidence doesn't exist or for hosted defaults.
00:10:34 Tom: will you put the SecureShare link in the CRM? makes it easier for legal to find.
00:10:40 Evelyn: yes CRM-GT-4721 will have the link and we'll send an email.
00:10:47 Priya: one tiny nit — on the pre-filled SIG you marked A14 as "N/A" but that's actually relevant to our service isolation question. Could you revisit?
00:10:55 Marco: noted, we'll re-evaluate A14 and update the sheet.
00:11:03 Evelyn: any final items?
00:11:06 Priya: no, that's it, thanks. We'll collaborate on the SIG spreadsheet and circle back.
00:11:12 Evelyn: thanks everyone, we'll share the bundle and follow up with the Private deep-dive scheduling options.
00:11:18 Tom: thanks.
00:11:20 Lena: thank you.
00:11:23 Marco: bye.

(end of transcript)

Notes: transcript has casual speech, occasional transcription swaps (Privet/Private, k v cache/KV cache). Evidence references: SOC2 PDF, CAIQ mapping CSV, SCIM attribute mapping, audit log sample (redacted), KMS integration checklist, encryption architecture diagram, signed artifact example (SHA256).
